prompt:
A 1000 kg car rounds a flat (unbanked) curve of radius 20 m at a constant speed of 14 m/s ($g=9.8\text{ m/s}^2$).

**(a)** Calculate the centripetal force required to keep the car on the curve.

**(b)** What force provides this centripetal force?

**(c)** Calculate the minimum coefficient of static friction between the tires and the road needed for the car to make the turn without skidding.

rubric.description: Correctly identifies static friction between the tires and road as the source of the centripetal force
Correctly sets up μN = Fc with N=mg to solve for μ

sampleResponse:
(a) Fc = mv^2/r = (1000)(14^2)/20 = (1000)(196)/20 = 9800 N.
(b) Static friction between the tires and the road provides this centripetal force.
(c) The maximum available friction force is μN = μmg. Setting this equal to the required centripetal force: μmg = mv^2/r, so μ = v^2/(rg) = 196/(20)(9.8) = 196/196 = 1.0.

prompt:
Two small spheres, with masses $m_1 = 8$ kg and $m_2 = 2$ kg, have their centers separated by 0.5 m ($G=6.674\times10^{-11}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2$).

**(a)** Calculate the gravitational force between the spheres.

**(b)** If the distance between the spheres is doubled to 1.0 m, calculate the new gravitational force.

**(c)** Express the ratio of the original force (part a) to the new force (part b), and explain why this ratio makes sense given the inverse-square nature of gravity.

rubric.description: Correctly computes F = Gm1m2/r^2 ≈ 4.27×10^-9 N at r=0.5 m
Correctly recomputes F at r=1.0 m, getting ≈ 1.07×10^-9 N
Correctly computes the ratio of the two forces as 4:1 (or 4)
Correctly explains the ratio using the inverse-square law: doubling distance reduces force by a factor of 2^2=4

sampleResponse:
(a) F = Gm1m2/r^2 = (6.674×10^-11)(8)(2)/(0.5)^2 = (6.674×10^-11)(16)/0.25 ≈ 4.27×10^-9 N.
(b) At r=1.0 m: F = (6.674×10^-11)(16)/(1.0)^2 ≈ 1.07×10^-9 N.
(c) The ratio is 4.27×10^-9/1.07×10^-9 = 4. This makes sense because gravity follows an inverse-square law (F ∝ 1/r^2); doubling the distance should reduce the force by a factor of 2^2 = 4, which matches.

prompt:
A satellite orbits Earth (mass $M = 5.97\times10^{24}$ kg) in a circular orbit of radius $6.8\times10^6$ m ($G=6.674\times10^{-11}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2$).

**(a)** Derive an expression for the orbital speed $v$ in terms of $G$, $M$, and $r$, by setting the gravitational force equal to the required centripetal force.

**(b)** Calculate the satellite's orbital speed.

**(c)** Calculate the satellite's orbital period, in minutes.

rubric.description: Correctly sets GMm/r^2 = mv^2/r and simplifies (canceling the satellite's mass m) to get v = sqrt(GM/r)
Correctly computes the orbital period using T = 2πr/v
Correctly converts to get T ≈ 93 minutes

sampleResponse:
(a) Setting gravitational force equal to centripetal force: GMm/r^2 = mv^2/r. The satellite's mass m cancels from both sides: GM/r = v^2, so v = sqrt(GM/r).
(b) v = sqrt[(6.674×10^-11)(5.97×10^24)/(6.8×10^6)] ≈ 7650 m/s.
(c) T = 2πr/v = 2π(6.8×10^6)/7650 ≈ 5582 s. Converting to minutes: 5582/60 ≈ 93 minutes.
